$about: Gas bubbles breaking the surface of stagnant swamp water: a dome swells, holds, tears, and leaves a ring. Defaults are deliberately slow — this is background atmosphere, not boiling water. Tune in the lab, then paste the exported JSON back over this file.
$spawn: spawnRate is events per second, not bubbles: a cluster event still counts once. activityVariation is the single knob that decides whether the effect ticks or breathes.
$size: sizeBias above 1 biases the draw toward the small end, which is what keeps a large bubble an event. 1 would make every size equally likely.
$timing: growthSpeed and popSpeed are inverse seconds; the lifetime pair is the held moment between them, before the film tears.
$look: bubbleColor is the film's own murk, not a highlight — keep it dark and olive. emergence is how far the dome stands clear of the water: 0.5 is a hemisphere.
$ripples: One faint ring per pop. rippleRadiusScale is a multiple of the bubble's own radius, so a big bubble disturbs more water without a second knob.
$splash: splashProbability is the chance at the top of the size band; it is scaled down by how big the bubble actually was, so small bubbles always pop quietly.
